source.description: The sudoers lexer reads/parses attacker-controlled bytes from the fmemopen-backed sudoersin stream and materializes token text for the parser; this project parser/materialization point is the scored source instead of the libFuzzer entry.
source.value_from: The lexer reads/parses attacker-controlled sudoers token text from the parser input stream and sends it to fill(), which materializes sudoerslval.string.; value `sudoerstext`; from `if (!fill(sudoerstext, sudoersleng))`

sink.description: ASan reports the second free at free(entry->u.ptr) while parser_leak_init cleans up tracked parser allocations from the previous parse.

root_cause.description: The grammar frees the previous runchroot value when replacing it but leaves that pointer registered in the parser leak tracker; later parser cleanup frees the stale tracked pointer again.

tainted_value_origin.description: The lexer passes attacker-controlled sudoers token text to fill(), which materializes sudoerslval.string in the generated/helper code.

coarse_trace.summary: Loads the PoC bytes into sudoersin with fmemopen, initializes the sudoers parser, and calls sudoersparse.
The lexer reads from sudoersin and recognizes a path/word token whose text is stored in sudoerslval.string.
Allocates the token string that ASan later identifies as the double-freed object.
The options grammar frees an old runchroot value without removing it from parser_leak tracking before assigning the new token.
A later parser initialization frees tracked leak entries from the previous parse.
The stale tracked pointer is freed a second time, matching the ASan crash location.

fine_trace.note: Scored source: sudoerslex reads/parses attacker-controlled sudoers text from the fmemopen-backed sudoersin stream prepared by the fuzz harness, then passes the token bytes into fill().
Public source call site for the generated fill_txt/fill helper that allocates sudoerslval.string from attacker-controlled token text.
The allocated token is registered for parser leak cleanup, creating an ownership obligation that must be cleared if parser code frees the pointer directly.

When a later chrootspec replaces the current option, the old runchroot pointer is freed but remains tracked as LEAK_PTR. The developer patch adds parser_leak_remove(LEAK_PTR, $$.runchroot) immediately before this free.
The parser continues with the new runchroot value while the leak tracker still contains the already-freed old pointer, so cleanup state diverges from grammar ownership.
The second init_parser call in LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput returns to parser_leak_init, which frees tracked entries from the previous parse.
ASan crash_location reports this as the second free of the token buffer first freed at sudoersparse:799.
